# Achilleús: the stories first, then the spelling

You cannot weigh an accent without knowing what it carries. Here is what **Achilleús** has been carrying.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**Two Fates, Weighed Aloud.** Book 9 of the Iliad stages the first great decision scene of Western literature.  Agamemnon's embassy — Odysseus, Aias, and old Phoinix, bearing the offer of treasure, one of Agamemnon's daughters, and restored honor — finds Achilleús in his tent, singing “the famous deeds of men” to his lyre (9. 186–189).

**The Death of Patroklos.** When Patroklos begged to enter the fighting in Achilleús' armor, the hero warned him: drive the Trojans from the ships and come back — do not press on to Troy (16. 87–96).  Patroklos drove them, pressed on, and Hektōr killed him in the borrowed armor, prophesying with his dying breath that Achilleús would soon die beneath the same wall (16.

**Paris' Arrow, the Heel.** The Iliad never tells Achilleús' death; it keeps only arranging the appointment.  Hektōr, dying, foretells it — “the day will come when Paris and Phoibos Apóllōn destroy you at the Scaean gates” (22. 358–360) — and the hero himself tells the doomed Lykāon that not even he will come home (21.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **Ἀχιλλεύς**, in the attestation Homer, Iliad 1.1–7; 9.182–668; 16.87–854; 18.23–126, 468–613; 22.358–360, 395–404; 24.468–676 and Proclus, Chrestomathy (summary of the lost Cypria: the death of Achilles) give us. The name means "Possibly 'grief of the people' (from ἄχος + λαός), or a pre-Greek name".

The restoration keeps one feature the ASCII form *achilleus* cannot show:

- **u → ú** — Stress mark (acute/tone): where the voice peaks.

A storyteller pronouncing the name would restore every one of them by instinct. The file only writes down what the voice already knows.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Achilleús
- **ASCII form:** achilleus
- **Meaning:** "Possibly 'grief of the people' (from ἄχος + λαός), or a pre-Greek name"
- **Domain of influence:** War, Glory, Rage
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἀχιλλεύς
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 4 of 546

## The Name Travels

Rome read him through the Aeneid's mirror: Achilles is what Aeneas must not be — brilliant, doomed, and defiant of fate.  Alexander the Great slept with the Iliad under his pillow and ran a victory lap around Achilleús' supposed tomb at Troy, consciously modelling his own short bright career on the hero's choice; his successors commissioned the Alexandrian portraiture of Achilles as the template of royal arete.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Achilleús** stands at [/achilleus/](/achilleus/) — [lore](/achilleus/lore/), [scholars](/achilleus/scholars/), [patterns](/achilleus/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. What survives here cannot be shown in ASCII: a feature of the original that the fallback alphabet flattens. That is the Tier-1 test, and this name passes it without argument.

## The Sources Are Open

The myths above are retold from the temple's record; the primary voices are in the [Sacred Texts](/texts/): [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/). Nothing in this file outranks them.
